overview: The Community Development Board serves as Medford's planning board, responsible for reviewing site plans, special permits, subdivision plans, and Approval Not Required (ANR) lot divisions, while also advising the City Council on comprehensive zoning recodification. The archive spans 50 meetings from June 2024 through October 2026. Across this period, the board transitioned from evaluating individual site plans and corridor zonings to conducting major joint public hearings with the City Council on square and corridor district overhauls. Most recently, the board reviewed draft citywide zoning cleanup amendments regarding formatting, height definitions, and development incentives, and approved a site plan modification on Mystic Avenue.

threads.name: Commercial and Transit Corridor Rezoning
threads.summary: Beginning in mid-2024, the board and planning staff reviewed corridor-level zoning updates to align key roadways with the city's Comprehensive Plan, recommending the Mystic Avenue Corridor District zoning amendments in December 2024. In March 2025, the board voted to recommend the Salem Street Corridor zoning amendments, later adjusting an intersection node back to Mixed Use 1. Throughout mid-2026, the board held joint hearings with the City Council on the Boston Avenue Neighborhood Corridor District, establishing subdistricts and student housing rules before forwarding a final amended recommendation in September 2026. Work on corridors continues through broader zoning consultant planning and citywide cleanup discussions.

threads.name: Medford Square and West Medford Square Rezoning
threads.summary: The board initiated discussions on rezoning commercial squares in mid-2025 to create mixed-use districts, establish daylight standards, and set tiered height incentives. Joint public hearings with the City Council commenced in early 2026 to refine subdistrict maps, parking flexibility, and historic preservation incentives. In March 2026, the board recommended approval of the City Hall Overlay District for the Transom development project while extending reviews on general square rules. As of late 2026, the broader square rezoning remains on the city's multi-year zoning timeline.

threads.name: Citywide Residential Zoning and ADU Overhaul
threads.summary: Starting in late 2024 and continuing into early 2025, the board reviewed comprehensive neighborhood and urban residential zoning proposals and new state mandates for accessory dwelling units (ADUs). Following multiple informational sessions, public hearings drew extensive testimony regarding infrastructure capacity, building heights, and tree protection. In mid-2025, the City Council and board opted to table certain elements and schedule deliberations toward a 2026 timeline. In late 2026, the board returned to citywide residential adjustments through inclusionary housing fractional payment recommendations and incentive bonus calculations.

threads.name: Tufts University Campus and Institutional Zoning
threads.summary: The board reviewed educational uses under the Dover Amendment, evaluating Tufts University's 10-story student housing project at 401 Boston Avenue beginning in late 2024. In February 2025, the board approved the site plan with reporting requirements on shuttles, police calls, and a neighborhood improvement fund. Concurrently, the board held information sessions in May 2025 to draft a dedicated institutional zoning district to regulate campus building heights and setbacks. In 2026, the board and City Council agreed not to rush the institutional zoning ordinance, scheduling drafting and consultant procurement for subsequent terms.

threads.name: Dover Amendment and Shelter Reviews
threads.summary: In November 2024, the board received a Dover Amendment site plan application to convert a former convent at 21 St. Clair Road into an educational shelter for women and children. Over several meetings, the board explored Dover Amendment eligibility, legal authority, neighbor outreach, and traffic and parking impacts. Municipal counsel was consulted regarding board authority under the Dover Amendment in late 2024. The board approved the site plan review with conditions governing resident vehicle limits, off-street parking, and shuttles in January 2025.

threads.name: Subdivision Oversight and Covenants
threads.summary: The board routinely evaluates definitive subdivisions, roadway extensions, and associated financial security. For the Bridal Path subdivision off Franklin Avenue, the board continued hearings through late 2024 and early 2025 before approving the definitive plan with blasting prohibitions, eventually endorsing the plan and replacing covenants with a tripartite agreement. The board also approved covenant releases and roadway extensions for the Mary Kenny Way subdivision in March 2025. ANR lot divisions and subdivision oversight continue on a regular application basis.

threads.name: Community Development Block Grant Performance Reviews
threads.summary: Acting in its public reporting capacity, the board conducts annual hearings on the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Consolidated Annual Performance Evaluation Report (CAPER). In September 2025, the board held a public hearing reviewing $1.1 million in prior program expenditures. In September 2026, the board convened the subsequent annual hearing detailing completed sidewalk and housing rehabilitation projects and previewing upcoming playground designs and neighborhood revitalization strategies.
